problem.statement: WPF developers cannot diagnose why binding a Command through a non-INotifyPropertyChanged parent class's property to an INPC child causes objects to be retained (leaked) across window open/close cycles, and have no tooling to pinpoint the root cause.

persona.primary: WPF/.NET developer debugging memory leaks in a legacy desktop application

context.situation: A developer noticed repeated window open/close cycles retaining objects when a Command binding chains through a non-INPC parent to an INPC child property, and turned to a public forum for an explanation since nothing pinpointed the root cause.

possible_wedges.offer: A WPF binding/leak analyzer that inspects live or static binding expressions and flags non-INPC-parent-to-INPC-child command binding patterns known to cause CommandManager retention.
A static analyzer CLI that scans XAML and code-behind for command bindings routed through non-INPC intermediate properties and reports likely leak sites.
A Visual Studio extension that highlights this specific WPF anti-pattern inline during code review.

risks: Single evidence item with no corroborating reports, so demand signal is very thin.
Signals show low commercial intent (0.1) and zero commitment; the asker wanted an explanation, not a tool.
No workaround or existing substitute was mentioned, suggesting a knowledge gap rather than a tooling gap.
This CommandManager/WeakEventManager leak pattern is a well-documented WPF pitfall already explained in existing blog posts and SO answers, which may satisfy the need for free.
Persona and use case (one-off debugging question) may not generalize to a broader audit-tooling market.

cheapest_experiment.hypothesis: WPF developers who hit this specific command-binding retention pattern will submit their code for a free automated/manual leak check rather than just wanting a text explanation.
cheapest_experiment.input: Reply on the original thread and similar WPF memory-leak Q&A threads offering a free check: paste your ViewModel/XAML binding snippet and get a report flagging leak-prone binding paths.
cheapest_experiment.output: A short manual or lightly-automated leak-pattern report delivered by email.
cheapest_experiment.commitment_event: Developer submits their code snippet and email address for the check.
cheapest_experiment.success_threshold: 5+ submissions across 5-10 similar threads within 2 weeks.
cheapest_experiment.failure_threshold: 1 or fewer submissions after posting on 5+ similar threads.
